title: How does the shortest XY compare with the side AB?
description: The shortest length of the line joining the two moving points is measured at several level positions and compared with the side AB, which is seven centimetres. Keeko's doubt is that a line drawn inside the rectangle must be shorter than the side.
teaching_notes: One idea: the level XY always equals AB, because both sit between the same two parallel sides. Watch for students who think a line drawn inside a rectangle must be shorter than the side.

source: How does the minimum distance between the points X and Y com
video_script.why: A learner compares the shortest length of XY with the side AB of the rectangle.
video_script.substitution: the book's own rectangle with AB seven centimetres, and the level positions of its two moving points
video_script.anchor: a rectangle with a point X on one side and a point Y on the opposite side, joined by a level line
video_script.wrong_answer: the line drawn inside the rectangle must be shorter than the side
video_script.wrong_move: believes a line drawn inside the rectangle has to be shorter than the side it runs beside
video_script.payoff_line: The shortest ex why is exactly as long as eigh bee.

final_answer.value: The minimum distance of XY is 7 cm, equal to AB
final_answer.spoken: exactly as long as eigh bee

maths_rules: XY is shortest when X and Y are level (equal distances from A and B)
level XY = 7 cm at one centimetre, two centimetres and every other level position
AD and BC are both perpendicular to AB, so they stay 7 cm apart everywhere, hence level XY = AB = 7 cm
video_script.design: The level line is drawn and measured at two positions, each time beside AB, then compared.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about the same rectangle.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The side eigh bee is seven centimetres, and ex why joins the two moving points.
How does the shortest ex why compare with eigh bee?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: rectangle ABCD with X and Y level, at equal distances from A and B

marks.short: X and Y sit level with each other
marks.plan: a ruler is laid along XY

narration: <bookmark mark='short'/>Ex why is shortest when ex and why are level with each other.
That means they are at the same distance from eigh and bee.
<bookmark mark='plan'/>We measure ex why at two level positions and compare it with eigh bee.

beats.on_screen: Given: AB = 7 cm; X and Y level
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eigh bee is seven centimetres, and ex and why are level.

beats.on_screen: To find: how the shortest XY compares with AB

marks.find: the question is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to compare the shortest ex why with eigh bee.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: X and Y level at 1 cm from A and B; XY = 7 cm

marks.first: X and Y are placed level, one centimetre up, and XY is measured as 7 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, place ex and why level, one centimetre from eigh and bee. Ex why measures seven centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: X and Y level at 2 cm from A and B; XY = 7 cm again

marks.second: X and Y are moved level to two centimetres up, and XY is measured as 7 cm again

narration: <bookmark mark='second'/>Step two, move both points level to two centimetres, and measure again. Ex why is seven centimetres again.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the shortest XY is 7 cm, equal to AB

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The shortest ex why is exactly as long as eigh bee.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the rectangle
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the two upright sides marked 7 cm apart at the bottom and at the top, with the level line between them

marks.doubt: the level line inside the rectangle is shown with a question mark
marks.fix: double arrows show the two upright sides 7 cm apart at two heights
marks.keep: the level line fills the gap and matches the base

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the line drawn inside the rectangle must be shorter than the side.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the two upright sides are perpendicular to the base, so they stay seven centimetres apart everywhere.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>A level line between them spans that whole gap, so it is seven centimetres too.
